t: I believe {part|some} of it. I am still working out which part.
That could be {god}. It could also be people filling in the gaps.
I want to take your word for it. Give me a little time.
You sound certain. I wish certainty passed between people that easily.
I am not dismissing it. I am trying not to rush into believing it.
Maybe that is what happened. I cannot say it as firmly as you can.
Part of me believes you already. The rest is being stubborn.
I have changed my mind twice while you were speaking.
That sounds true until I try to explain it to myself.
I will say maybe today. Ask me again {tomorrow|after I sleep}.
I do not think you are lying. I am less sure about what it means.
There might be something to it. That is as far as I can go.
Start again from the beginning. I missed something.
Who told you first? That usually matters.
I had not heard that. I am glad you told me.
That explains what everyone was whispering about {this morning|by the fire}.
I need to think before I answer that properly.
You have my attention. Keep going.
I heard a different version, but yours makes more sense.
That is going to spread before supper.
Have you seen how far we walk for a straight tree now?
I spent more time hauling than cutting today.
The axe head is loose again. I tightened it this morning.
There is good timber {past the creek|over the ridge}, but the ground is miserable.
I found rot in three trunks today. They looked sound from outside.
We should leave the young stand alone for another season.
The woodpile looked low when I passed it. Did you notice?
One of the new saplings has taken well. The others need water.
I could hear your tree come down from the ridge.
The far stand is better wood, but it adds {hours|half a day} of carrying.
My hands are still shaking from that last trunk.
I sharpened this axe yesterday, and the edge is already gone.
We need a better path before we go any farther out.
I saw the rot too. Mark those trees before somebody trusts one.
The pile will hold if tomorrow goes well.
Leave the saplings. We will need them later.
I will take the far side tomorrow. You work near the creek.
We should bring rope next time. That slope is asking for trouble.
I will mark the sound trunks before dark.
The hauling is the part nobody counts until their back hurts.
I will see you at the woodpile before supper.
Let us finish the close stand before we argue about the far one.
Bring the wedge tomorrow. Mine is nearly done.
We can settle it after we count what came in today.
